chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Jama'ah ibn Sa'd al-Khath'ami, that he said:

Al-Mufaddal was with Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام, so Al-Mufaddal said to him: “May I be sacrificed for you, would Allah obligate the obedience of a servant upon the servants and withhold from him the news of the heaven?”

He عليه السلام said: “No. Allah is more generous, more merciful, and more compassionate toward His servants than to obligate the obedience of a servant upon the servants and then withhold from him the news of the heaven, morning and evening.”

key_terms.أَرْأَفُ: more compassionate and tender toward His servants
key_terms.أَكْرَمُ: more generous and noble in dealing with creation
key_terms.الْعِبَادِ: the servants of Allah who are addressed with obedience
key_terms.خَبَرَ السَّمَاءِ: knowledge or report from the heaven

ai.seo_question: Would Allah make obedience to an Imam obligatory while withholding heavenly knowledge from him?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms that if Allah makes obedience to a person obligatory over people, He does not leave that person cut off from heavenly knowledge. It presents this as a matter of Allah’s generosity, mercy, and compassion toward His servants, and it is used in the context of the Imam’s divinely granted knowledge.
